1519549380791631903.name: meeting-notes
1519549380791631903.description: This channel lives in SPECIAL INTEREST GROUPS and serves as the central archive for meeting notes across Protocol Institute's various discussion groups and ad hoc sessions. Posts here are transcriptions and summaries of live conversations—ranging from technical deep dives (ML accelerators, APIs) to conceptual seminars (history, path dependence, publishing workflows)—organized by date and topic. Follow this channel to catch up on what different groups are exploring, or post notes from your own meetings.
1519549380791631903.guide_blurb: Meeting notes & transcripts from Protocol Institute discussion groups

1082444652659093506.name: introductions-mod
1082444652659093506.description: A moderator-only channel for server setup discussions and administrative coordination. This is not a public channel for member introductions despite its name—it's where admins discuss onboarding processes, gatekeeping mechanisms, and server configuration. Members should not post here unless explicitly invited by moderators.
1082444652659093506.guide_blurb: Mod-only setup channel. Members: use #introductions instead.

1082446020480352256.name: faq
1082446020480352256.description: This read-only archived channel contains frequently asked questions about the Protocol Institute, covering topics like role eligibility, program requirements, and membership policies. Questions and answers are posted by moderators and leadership to clarify common inquiries. The channel serves as a reference resource for new members seeking quick answers about participation and program expectations.
1082446020480352256.guide_blurb: Read-only FAQ resource with answers to common questions about roles and eligibility.

1082461541951078440.name: 📣-announcements
1082461541951078440.description: A high-volume announcement channel where C3P0 regularly shares new articles from Protocolized (the Institute's publication platform), and core team members post updates about workshops, server reorganizations, and major initiatives. The channel serves as the primary feed for staying current with the Institute's intellectual output and structural developments, with a consistent cadence of content releases covering protocol theory, fiction, AI, governance, and related topics.
1082461541951078440.guide_blurb: Follow for regular Protocolized article drops and major server updates.

1082461579150381116.name: ☀️-general
1082461579150381116.description: The main gathering space for Protocol Institute members to share research interests, coordinate on special interest groups (SIGs), discuss emerging work in governance and institutional design, and surface opportunities for collaboration across domains like blockchain, cities, AI, and web3. Posts range from casual research questions and event announcements to substantive discussions about protocol design, institutional innovation, and cross-sector connections. The tone is intellectually curious and collaborative, with members actively recruiting co-leads, soliciting feedback, and building projects together.
1082461579150381116.guide_blurb: General discussion hub for research, SIGs, event announcements & collaboration

1082461870578995212.name: 🎲-random
1082461870578995212.description: A general discussion space for sharing links, ideas, and spontaneous conversations across Protocol Institute interests. Members post research articles, project discoveries, technical tools, and questions—ranging from token design and water conservation to AI search, user experience, and emerging infrastructure. The channel has a low-friction, high-signal vibe where members crowdsource knowledge and flag interesting work for relevant communities.
1082461870578995212.guide_blurb: Share links, discoveries, and quick questions with the broader Protocol community.

1082489747777261608.name: welcome
1082489747777261608.description: This read-only archived channel serves as the server's entry point, containing the initial welcome message and onboarding instructions for new members joining the Protocol Institute community. It was used during the Summer of Protocols event to direct users through a rules agreement process before gaining access to the main server. This is where Protocol Institute leadership communicates the server's purpose and guides members through their first steps.
1082489747777261608.guide_blurb: Read-only channel with server welcome & onboarding—no posting here.

1082500625478201405.name: rules
1082500625478201405.description: The #rules channel establishes foundational guidelines and expectations for the Protocol Institute Discord community. New members should review this channel to understand server conduct standards, onboarding procedures (like introducing yourself in designated channels and setting display names), and community norms. This is primarily a read-only reference space where server moderators post authoritative information rather than a discussion channel.
1082500625478201405.guide_blurb: Read #rules first—it explains onboarding steps and community expectations.

1082500625478201407.name: moderator-only
1082500625478201407.description: This is a moderator-exclusive channel for administrative discussion and community management updates. It receives official announcements from Discord's Community Updates bot about platform changes, server features, and moderation tools, along with occasional informal exchanges between moderators. New members should not post here unless they have been granted moderator privileges.
1082500625478201407.guide_blurb: Mod-only channel for administrative updates & team coordination.

1082504762433490975.name: 👋-introductions
1082504762433490975.topic: Use this channel to introduce yourself to the rest of the Summer of Protocols community. See the pinned post for an introduction outline.
1082504762433490975.description: A welcoming space where Summer of Protocols community members introduce themselves, sharing their backgrounds, expertise, and reasons for joining. Posts range from brief hellos to detailed descriptions of work in governance, protocol engineering, AI/ML, and adjacent fields. The channel serves as a low-pressure entry point where newcomers—whether seasoned researchers, curious lurkers, or book club participants—can signal their presence and connect with others.
1082504762433490975.guide_blurb: Introduce yourself here! Share who you are and what drew you to the community.

1083785358363336846.name: application-feedback
1083785358363336846.topic: Use this channel if to get feedback on your SoP application or project.
1083785358363336846.description: This archived channel served as a space for applicants to receive constructive feedback on their Statement of Purpose (SoP) applications and project ideas before submission. Members asked clarifying questions about program scope (e.g., whether political applications were acceptable), got suggestions for strengthening their proposals, and received logistical updates from moderators. The tone is collaborative and intellectually curious, with experienced members offering concrete revision advice.
1083785358363336846.guide_blurb: Archived feedback channel for SoP applications—check for similar active channels.

1083808989961261076.name: links-for-reading-list
1083808989961261076.topic: Please post any links here that you think should go in our reading list database https://efdn.notion.site/0314a1800b774258a8e6197487c479bc?v=15fb6b39a490413cbba3b7f78ad67c2b
1083808989961261076.description: A read-only archive channel for curating links to high-quality resources relevant to protocol research and theory. Contributors share academic papers, essays, books, and articles spanning economics, governance, decentralized systems, fiction, and philosophy—with an intellectual tone that values clarity, rigor, and cross-disciplinary connections. All submissions feed into a centralized Notion reading list database.
1083808989961261076.guide_blurb: Archive of curated protocol-related reading materials; browsing only.

1084135714830164100.name: 🤔-idle-protocol-musings
1084135714830164100.topic: Channel to think out loud and shitpost about protocols, and sharpen your concepts by playing with them.
1084135714830164100.description: A space for exploring protocol concepts through experimental thinking, loose speculation, and conceptual play. Members here range from theorists to practitioners—branding experts, protocol researchers, AI systems thinkers—who use the channel to stress-test ideas, make unexpected connections, and sharpen intuitions. The vibe is intellectual but irreverent: shitposting about serious concepts, following tangents, asking 'am I crazy?' questions, and building on each other's musings without requiring polished conclusions.
1084135714830164100.guide_blurb: Think out loud about protocols & adjacent ideas; connective, exploratory, often half-baked.

1084876704918536233.name: take-an-idea-leave-an-idea
1084876704918536233.topic: A channel to drop ideas for projects you may not want to pursue OR find an idea if you can’t think of one yourself.  Non-crypto project ideas especially encouraged.
1084876704918536233.description: An archived read-only channel where Protocol Institute members deposited project ideas they weren't pursuing or browsed for inspiration. The conversation evolved into theoretical discussion about protocol design principles—symmetry, regularity, aperiodicity, and what constitutes 'good' vs 'bad' protocols. Populated by researchers exploring cross-disciplinary connections between protocols, physics, biology, and institutional design.
1084876704918536233.guide_blurb: Archived ideas channel with deep theoretical threads on protocol design principles.

1088124124968259584.name: 🙋-channel-proposals
1088124124968259584.topic: Post ideas for new channels here, upvote ideas to get them realized, and start threads for discussion if needed.
1088124124968259584.description: This channel is for proposing and discussing new channels that might serve the community. Members upvote ideas they support and start threads to develop proposals collaboratively. The conversation tends toward practical questions about server organization, preventing channel proliferation while accommodating diverse research workflows and community needs.
1088124124968259584.guide_blurb: Post channel ideas here and upvote ones you'd find useful.

1089036778507341874.name: protocol-candidates
1089036778507341874.topic: A place to drop links with brief argument about why it should be considered a protocol. Submissions may or may not be added to the protocols index depending on whether the argument is compelling or not.
1089036778507341874.description: A read-only archive where community members submit links and arguments for potential protocols—anything from social conventions (roommate door signals, parallel parking) to formal standards (UN statistics recommendations, passport systems). The channel hosts exploratory, intellectually curious discussion about what constitutes a protocol across domains: from human behavior and organizational structures to ecological management and international agreements. Posts range from pop culture references to academic curiosities, united by the question of whether something can be understood as a protocol worth documenting.
1089036778507341874.guide_blurb: Browse submissions & arguments for protocol candidates across culture, systems & nature.

1090292237423870122.name: meta-analysis
1090292237423870122.topic: A channel to discuss basic definitions and distinctions.
1090292237423870122.description: A read-only archive channel hosting deep conceptual discussions about protocols, their definitions, and their relationships to adjacent frameworks like game theory, complexity, and organizational structures. The conversation is highly technical and theoretical, drawing on examples from warfare, APIs, and social organization to explore what distinguishes protocols as a category. Participants include @_vgr, @_ergod, @doriantaylor, and @rafa_0x engaging in Socratic dialogue about protocol ontology, protocolization equilibrium, and the vertical/horizontal distinctions between protocol and game theory.
1090292237423870122.guide_blurb: Archived conceptual deep-dives on protocol definitions and theory — read-only reference.

1090752622031536189.name: reading-room
1090752622031536189.topic: Create a post with your reading list link and title it with either the name of the reading or a very brief description. Use the emoji reaction to 'upvote' interesting readings.
1090752622031536189.description: The #reading-room is an archived, read-only forum where members curate and share their personal reading lists. Posts feature curated collections of books, papers, and articles with titles or brief descriptions, and the community uses emoji reactions to highlight the most valuable or interesting readings. This channel serves as a searchable repository of intellectual resources recommended by Protocol Institute members across various domains.
1090752622031536189.guide_blurb: Browse curated reading lists from community members; use reactions to flag favorites.

1093581722538496122.name: core-chat
1093581722538496122.description: An archived read-only channel documenting the real-time conversation around a collaborative writing project on protocols. Members discuss manuscript progress, word counts, editing challenges, and share work-in-progress links. The tone is informal and self-aware, with playful meta-commentary about Goodhart's Law and strategic use of the word 'protocol' itself.
1093581722538496122.guide_blurb: Archived discussion of a collaborative protocol writing project—browse for context on past work.

1093581771460845628.name: researcher-support
1093581771460845628.description: This archived channel documents the final phases of Summer of Protocols 2023, capturing logistical coordination, citation methodology discussions, and feedback exchanges among researchers finalizing their work. The conversation reflects a collaborative academic environment where participants navigate practical challenges (formatting, citations, file management) while supporting each other's research completion. The tone is casual but intellectually engaged, mixing technical problem-solving with substantive peer review.
1093581771460845628.guide_blurb: Read-only archive of SoP 2023 final submissions and production logistics.

1095024498249580597.name: ⭐-popular-posts
1095024498249580597.topic: This channel to surface popular posts and conversations. Any post in this server that accumulates the required number of ⭐️ will be listed in this channel.
1095024498249580597.description: A curated feed of community highlights automatically surfaced from across the server. When posts in other channels accumulate 3+ star reactions from members, Dyno posts a link here, creating a living record of conversations the community found most valuable. This channel helps members discover quality discussions they might have missed and see what resonates most with the Protocol Institute community.
1095024498249580597.guide_blurb: Follow for highlights & trending discussions across the server—curated by community reactions.

1095846506382250075.name: 🔍-protocol-watch
1095846506382250075.topic: news about real protocols in the wild
1095846506382250075.description: A casual, wide-ranging observation channel for spotting protocols operating in the real world—from software stacks and infrastructure to social choreography, institutional designs, and physical systems. Members share news, links, and field notes about how protocols work in practice, debating what counts as a protocol and how they enable or constrain behavior. The vibe is exploratory and interdisciplinary rather than prescriptive, mixing technical depth with social and material observations.
1095846506382250075.guide_blurb: Found a real-world protocol in action? Share it here for collaborative spotting.

1097633612955914340.name: field-reports
1097633612955914340.topic: channel to post photos and first-hand field reports of protocol relevant observed things. No opinion or news. Off-topic posts will be deleted.
1097633612955914340.description: A read-only archive channel for posting photographs and first-hand field reports of observations relevant to Protocol Institute research. Content is strictly factual documentation without opinion, analysis, or news commentary. Posts document infrastructure patterns, organizational phenomena, economic structures, and systems-level observations that relate to the institute's investigative interests.
1097633612955914340.guide_blurb: Read-only archive of field observations & photos. No opinions—just factual reports.

1100181437841416293.name: pilot-study
1100181437841416293.description: Archive of the Protocol Institute's pilot study initiative from May-July 2023. Contains collaborative research discussions, breakout session notes, and evolving definitions of what constitutes a protocol across domains (technical systems, social structures, organizational boundaries). Contributors share Google Doc annotations, conceptual frameworks (protocol phenomenology, declarative vs. procedural), and real-world applications while developing core pilot study outputs.
1100181437841416293.guide_blurb: Read-only archive of pilot study research & breakout discussions (May-July 2023)

1101266241932492830.name: wip-index
1101266241932492830.topic: Channel for sharing links to work-in-public/work-in-progress updates on core research projects from core researchers’ personal newsletters etc. Other content will be deleted.
1101266241932492830.description: A curated feed of work-in-progress research updates from core Protocol Institute researchers sharing their public intellectual output. Posts are primarily links to personal newsletters, blog posts, technical notes, and essays on protocol-related topics, with occasional discussion threads. The channel maintains high signal by limiting content to active research updates from community members engaged in substantive, long-form thinking.
1101266241932492830.guide_blurb: Share links to your public research updates & WIP writing on protocols.

1102973331071828119.name: 🏙built-environment
1102973331071828119.description: A read-only archive documenting collaborative research on the built environment and address systems. Members share drafts, artifacts, and detailed feedback on essays exploring how physical space becomes computationally addressable—from apartment numbering conventions to the digitization of urban infrastructure. The channel captures iterative intellectual work with a focus on rigorous annotation and conceptual refinement.
1102973331071828119.guide_blurb: Archive of research on addressability in built environments and infrastructure.

1103065140942872587.name: protocol-town-hall
1103065140942872587.topic: This channel is dedicated to discussion around the guest talks and researcher salons. A forum post will be created for each guest talk and will include links to pre-reading, thoughts from Visiting Researchers pre-talk and general discourse about the talk and topics
1103065140942872587.description: This archived forum channel documents the Protocol Institute's guest talks and researcher salons, featuring curated discussion threads for each event. Each forum post includes pre-reading materials, insights from visiting researchers, and community discourse on the talk's themes and implications. The channel preserves intellectual conversations for reference and creates a structured record of the Institute's speaker programming and collaborative research salons.
1103065140942872587.guide_blurb: Browse recorded guest talks and researcher salon discussions with curated resources.

1103347728957833359.name: research-material-help
1103347728957833359.topic: Use this channel to request help with gaining access to gated research materials or other research material assistance
1103347728957833359.description: A read-only archived channel for requesting help accessing gated academic papers, research materials, and guidance on finding scholarly resources. Members post links to paywalled articles and ask for assistance locating them elsewhere, or seek recommendations on where to find literature on specific research topics. The community has a collaborative, peer-to-peer ethos with experienced researchers helping newer members navigate institutional access barriers and discover relevant sources.
1103347728957833359.guide_blurb: Request help finding paywalled papers or locate specific research materials.

1103521090606743603.name: 🚀-boost-zone
1103521090606743603.description: A curated space for sharing links and content aligned with Protocol Institute's interests—research articles, program announcements, relevant events, and work by community members. Posts here are intended for amplification across social networks and represent ideas or initiatives of long-term value to the community. The channel operates on light curation: contributions should connect to protocols, institutional thinking, or aligned events rather than arbitrary content.
1103521090606743603.guide_blurb: Share protocol-adjacent work & events worth amplifying across your networks.

1105208006414716978.name: test-of-protocolness
1105208006414716978.description: This archived channel documents collaborative efforts to define and identify what makes something a "protocol." Members brainstorm diagnostic tests, candidate definitions, and conceptual frameworks for protocol-nature, drawing on academic rigor and practical examples. The conversation balances philosophical precision with accessible language, featuring references to external writing and proposals for formalized concept schemes.
1105208006414716978.guide_blurb: Archived discussions on defining and testing what constitutes a protocol.

1106572787042238504.name: 👾-protocol-fiction
1106572787042238504.description: A specialized discussion channel for Protocol Fiction community members exploring experimental narrative forms, literary theory, and the intersection of AI-generated and human-authored fiction. Members engage in sophisticated textual analysis, debate aesthetic movements (hyperpop literature, grimdark new nature, stigmergic narratives), and examine technical writing innovations. The channel attracts literary-minded participants interested in avant-garde aesthetics, leitmotif theory, and how emerging technologies challenge traditional writing conventions.
1106572787042238504.guide_blurb: Literary theory & experimental narrative forms; theory-heavy, avant-garde focused.
1106572787042238504.cadence: Every 2 weeks on Thursday at 15:00 UTC

1107727857595203644.name: 🔧tech-standards
1107727857595203644.description: A read-only archive channel documenting technical discussions around protocols, standards, and knowledge systems. The conversation centers on naming conventions for technical tools, the dynamics of standards wars, and how protocol literacy shapes technological adoption. Posts include research links, video explanations, draft documents for feedback, and intellectual debates about whether standards optimization is premature or evolutionarily necessary.
1107727857595203644.guide_blurb: Archive of technical standards & protocol discussions — read-only reference.

1107728702378365008.name: 🧠unconscious-protocols
1107728702378365008.description: This archived channel documents an intellectual conversation about protocols as a conceptual framework, exploring how explicit protocols shape coordination, power dynamics, and social organization. Regular contributors engaged with interdisciplinary theory (Foucault, Durkheim, Vervaeke) while workshopping essays on protocols' social implications. The channel captures a collaborative research process where members shared drafts, cross-referenced ideas, and debated whether protocols themselves are neutral tools or inherently value-laden.
1107728702378365008.guide_blurb: Archived research discussion on protocols, power, and social coordination.

1107728758628159570.name: 🕸credit-protocols
1107728758628159570.description: A read-only archive channel documenting the development of a research essay on credit protocols and knowledge systems. Members share drafts, request feedback on writing, discuss conceptual frameworks like 'paradigm refugees' and 'populist paradigms,' and make connections to related Protocol Institute projects. The channel captures iterative scholarly work-in-progress with a focus on refining arguments about unadjudicated knowledge, corporate monopolies on intangibles, and systemic protocols.
1107728758628159570.guide_blurb: Archived research on credit protocols & knowledge systems—read to follow ongoing scholarship.

1107728832548589669.name: 🕯death-memory
1107728832548589669.description: An archived read-only channel documenting the Protocol Institute's research into death, memory, and temporal practices. Posts include scholarly references, project updates from the New Time Machines fellowship, shared articles on death rituals across cultures, and collaborative thinking around memory as a navigational and archival tool. The conversation blends academic rigor with speculative design, featuring researchers workshopping ideas, sharing sources, and developing memory-related protocols and physical artifacts.
1107728832548589669.guide_blurb: Archive of death & memory research — read only, for context on Institute's temporal work.

1107728906116665374.name: 🐝organizational-protocols
1107728906116665374.description: This archived channel documents collaborative research and essay development on organizational protocols, safety systems, and platform dynamics. Members discuss theoretical frameworks, share resources, and provide peer feedback on work-in-progress essays. The conversation reflects a scholarly community engaged in rigorous intellectual exchange about systems thinking, with participants critically examining definitions, assumptions, and real-world applications.
1107728906116665374.guide_blurb: Archived research collaboration on safety protocols & organizational systems.

1110602202822750359.name: kylebot
1110602202822750359.description: An archived channel documenting the development and experimentation of a Discord bot for categorizing and linking protocol-related content across the server. Technical discussions center on bot implementation, link curation workflows, and the broader challenge of knowledge management in community spaces. Contributors include the bot's creator Kyle Mathews and members experimenting with automated vs. manual content classification systems.
1110602202822750359.guide_blurb: Archived technical discussions on link curation bots & knowledge management.

1121118894795526164.name: researcher-meetings
1121118894795526164.topic: A channel for coordination the agenda for weekly researcher meetings.
1121118894795526164.description: This archived forum channel served as the coordination hub for setting agendas and organizing weekly researcher meetings at the Protocol Institute. Researchers would post discussion topics, research updates, and meeting logistics here before synchronous gatherings. The channel captures institutional memory about research priorities and collaborative planning, now preserved as read-only reference material.
1121118894795526164.guide_blurb: Archived coordination space for researcher meeting agendas—reference only.

1123770733819068577.name: kit-ops
1123770733819068577.topic: to coordinate kit production and publication
1123770733819068577.description: This archived channel documents the coordination of the School of Probable Futures kit production and publication strategy. Discussions cover design philosophy, release timelines, format specifications, printing logistics, and the vision for a modular binder system with official and community-contributed pages. The conversation balances practical production concerns with conceptual ambitions around scale, aesthetics, and long-term impact.
1123770733819068577.guide_blurb: Archive of kit production coordination—design, format, and release strategy discussions.

1124384276633362613.name: affiliate-chat
1124384276633362613.description: An archived read-only channel where Protocol Institute affiliates share project updates, coordinate working group sessions, and circulate work-in-progress artifacts for feedback. Posts include meeting reminders, calls for collaboration on protocol-related writing and research, links to shared documents and GitHub projects, and one-liner updates from affiliate meetings. The channel captures the collaborative rhythm of the affiliate program, with a focus on protocolization work across fiction, economics, timekeeping, and other domains.
1124384276633362613.guide_blurb: Read-only archive of affiliate project updates, meeting coordination, and WIP artifact sharing.

1125481632393072790.name: artifact-talk
1125481632393072790.description: A read-only archive documenting the collaborative development of the Protocol Institute's artifact collection. Members shared work-in-progress pieces, design iterations, and completed artifacts (visual essays, card games, chess variants, workshop kits) throughout the Summer of Protocols initiative. The channel captures the creative process, deadline discussions, and peer feedback as contributors refined conceptual and playable works exploring protocols and systems thinking.
1125481632393072790.guide_blurb: Archive of artifact development & peer feedback from the Summer of Protocols

1130156252870230057.name: impact-talk
1130156252870230057.description: Archive of high-level strategic discussions about the Protocol Institute's impact and field-building efforts. Members reflect on how to grow influence through protocols rather than institutions, debate the value of in-person convenings and institutional structures, and share research on creative collaboration and field dynamics. The tone is thoughtful and theoretical, anchored in readings from Derek de Solla Price, Open Philanthropy, and Michael Nielsen.
1130156252870230057.guide_blurb: Strategic meta-discussion on protocols, field-building, and institutional dynamics (read-only).

1133209585289793536.name: main-track
1133209585289793536.description: A read-only archive channel documenting the Protocol Institute's main retreat event from July 2023. Contains real-time discussion threads, creative references (architectural inspirations, literary allusions), collaborative project updates, and intellectual synthesis across participants—mixing practical logistics with speculative ideas about protocols, memory practices, and social systems. The channel captures the organic flow of a multi-day gathering where technical work, philosophical inquiry, and casual observations interweave.
1133209585289793536.guide_blurb: Archived retreat discussions—read to see how the community thinks through complex ideas together.

1133212468437581866.name: banter
1133212468437581866.topic: Use this channel for any off-topic conversation, activity coordination, or other unrelated banter during the SoP retreat.
1133212468437581866.description: A read-only archived channel documenting off-topic conversations and social coordination from the SoP retreat, including inside jokes (like the "Yahtzee" phone greeting), photo sharing protocols, personal reflections on the gathering, and casual banter about members' personalities. The channel captures the informal, playful intellectual culture of the community—mixing humor with thoughtful questions about ethics (image republication rights, emotional ergonomics of spaces) and collaborative memory-making. Posts are primarily from core retreat attendees sharing moments, coordinating activities, and building group identity through shared references.
1133212468437581866.guide_blurb: Archived retreat memories & inside jokes—read for community culture, don't post

1133625932029120572.name: link-bag
1133625932029120572.description: A curated collection of personal resource repositories where members maintain individual "link bags" — organized lists of useful links, articles, tools, and references discovered during conversations. Each member creates their own bag to share resources relevant to their interests and expertise. The channel serves as a living library where you can browse what others are collecting and get personalized recommendations based on individual curators.
1133625932029120572.guide_blurb: Browse curated personal link collections from community members.

1135604249376591952.name: protocol-visualization
1135604249376591952.description: A space for exploring visual and conceptual representations of protocols across multiple domains. Members share 3D designs, drawings, metaphors, and theoretical frameworks that help visualize how protocols operate—their surfaces, boundaries, and dynamics. The channel welcomes both artistic/speculative work and analytical diagrams, emphasizing generalizable insights over project-specific content.
1135604249376591952.guide_blurb: Share protocol visualizations, diagrams, and conceptual models—from 3D objects to drawings to metaphors.

1136367092573159575.name: protophernalia
1136367092573159575.description: An archived creative space for visualizing and playing with concepts from Protocol Institute discussions, particularly glossary terms and theoretical frameworks. Posts feature experimental definitions, conceptual art, and humorous coinages like 'Protocol Pickles' that explore tensions between competing ideas. The channel captures a playful yet intellectually rigorous vibe where members translate abstract protocol concepts into tangible or memorable forms.
1136367092573159575.guide_blurb: Visual & creative explorations of protocol theory concepts—read-only archive of past experiments.

1139397985122390058.name: 协议之夏
1139397985122390058.description: An archived discussion channel where Chinese-speaking and multilingual researchers explore the concept of "protocol" (协议) across humanities, social sciences, and governance contexts. The conversation centers on how protocols function differently across cultural and linguistic contexts, particularly examining implicit social protocols in Chinese culture versus Western legal/technical frameworks. Contributors engage in substantive theoretical debate about translation, methodology, and case studies, with discussions spanning media studies, history, bureaucratic systems, and emerging AI applications.
1139397985122390058.guide_blurb: Archived channel: multilingual protocol theory discussion with Chinese scholars

1327292074415882271.name: 🧑‍🎓-program-alumni
1327292074415882271.description: A read-only archive channel for Protocol Institute alumni to share updates on their ongoing research projects, conference participation, and collaborative opportunities. Posts reflect the community's interests in decentralized protocols, technical architecture, and emerging grant opportunities. The tone is informal and project-focused, with members sharing work-in-progress updates, seeking feedback on publications, and coordinating meetups around shared research interests.
1327292074415882271.guide_blurb: Alumni sharing project updates, conference leads, and research collaboration opportunities.

1327337414175490160.name: 🎩-formal-protocol-theory
1327337414175490160.description: A special interest group focused on formal protocol theory and design. Members discuss atomic protocol problems, multiagent systems, stigmergy, and related theoretical foundations. The channel features regular discussion sessions (SIGFPT calls), homework problems, and collaborative exploration of protocol-adjacent topics like supply chain security and agent coordination.
1327337414175490160.guide_blurb: Deep dives into protocol theory, multiagent systems & formal methods.
1327337414175490160.cadence: Every 2 weeks on Friday at 17:00 UTC

1327679519510888582.name: ✍️-writers-room
1327679519510888582.topic: For brainstorming and feedback on Protocolized drafts.
1327679519510888582.description: The #✍️-writers-room is an archived, read-only channel documenting the brainstorming and editorial feedback process for Protocolized written works. Members collaborate on drafts spanning essays, fiction, and theory pieces that explore how protocols shape culture, art, technology, and institutions. The channel captures the iterative development of publishable content, from conceptual debate through line-edits, with discussion of where pieces fit the Protocol Institute's intellectual mission.
1327679519510888582.guide_blurb: Read-only archive of draft feedback & essay development for Protocolized publications.

1333163344282124432.name: old-pitches-and-bounties
1333163344282124432.topic: Please use the new forum-style pitch channel.
1333163344282124432.description: This archived channel hosted story and essay pitches for Protocolized magazine, where editors like @_vgr provided feedback on protocol fiction concepts. Contributors pitched ideas ranging from blockchain horror to comedic takes on automated systems, with editors critiquing the strangeness and novelty of the proposed protocols. The channel has been deprecated in favor of a forum-style structure for better organization.
1333163344282124432.guide_blurb: Archived pitches channel—post new ideas in the forum instead.

1333851496416153702.name: 🚜-protocols-for-business
1333851496416153702.topic:
**Protocols for Business 101**

0) First time here? [Click here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1p0a-avfq1sZmmW5sJ2TtVMB1e83ig_zvHDCQ56XfKu8/edit?tab=t.0)
1) Start a thread with your protocol problems
2) Join the weekly discussion, on the [calendar](https://summerofprotocols.com/events)
3) Share an article on Protocols in the Business
4) Reach out to @rafa_0x with any questions (He's the group lead!)
1333851496416153702.description: This channel explores how protocols and decentralized systems reshape business operations, organizational structures, and work itself. Members discuss AI adoption patterns, context-building as economic value, org metabolism, and real-world implementation challenges across industries. The community includes builders, engineers, and strategists sharing research, live case studies, and theoretical frameworks.
1333851496416153702.guide_blurb: Join if you're thinking about protocols, AI, and org design through a business lens.
1333851496416153702.cadence: Every 2 weeks on Monday at 15:30 UTC

1337534941176795217.name: austin-meetup
1337534941176795217.description: A read-only archive documenting an Austin-based creative writing workshop where members experiment with AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, o1) to develop science fiction narratives. The channel captures iterative feedback on worldbuilding, character development, and plot structure, with discussions spanning tool selection, writing methodology, and craft critique. Posts reflect a collaborative, technically sophisticated community interested in both the creative process and the capabilities/limitations of current AI systems.
1337534941176795217.guide_blurb: Archive of AI-assisted sci-fi writing workshop with tool experimentation & craft feedback

1349790740418662531.name: 👽-scifi-contest
1349790740418662531.topic:
For brainstorming support and swapping ideas with competitors!

Learn more about the contest at: https://protocolized.summerofprotocols.com/p/terminological-twists
1349790740418662531.description: This archived channel served as the hub for the Protocol Institute's sci-fi writing contests, particularly the 'Ghosts in Machines' competition. It hosted real-time updates on submission deadlines, finalist announcements, judging processes, and community voting, while also facilitating peer support and technical questions from contest participants. The tone is informal and encouraging, with moderators providing transparency about decision-making and maintaining active engagement with the writing community.
1349790740418662531.guide_blurb: Archived contest hub—follow for past sci-fi writing competition updates & community discussions.

1361744073488203897.name: 📚-sop25
1361744073488203897.topic: Private channel for SoP25 to coordinate, collaborate, congregate, etc.
1361744073488203897.description: This archived channel documents the coordination and collaborative work of SoP25, a curriculum development group focused on teaching pedagogy and protocol instruction. Members discuss teaching methodologies, share pedagogical resources and quotes, coordinate synchronous meetings, and develop curriculum materials. The intellectual tone is reflective and practice-oriented, blending educational theory with experiential teaching challenges.
1361744073488203897.guide_blurb: Archive of SoP25's curriculum development coordination and teaching methodology discussions.

1366863858886774894.name: edge-esmeralda
1366863858886774894.description: This archived channel documents coordination and discussion around Edge Esmeralda 2025, a Protocol Institute gathering. Content includes logistical planning (flights, bike reservations, session scheduling), workshop brainstorming (Weathering Protocols, water treatment systems, technoscientific field building), and post-event reflections. The conversation reflects a thoughtful, systems-oriented community interested in long-term thinking, infrastructure resilience, and speculative futures.
1366863858886774894.guide_blurb: Archived event coordination & workshop discussions from Edge Esmeralda 2025 gathering.

1377504224421871616.name: 🧑‍🏫-curriculum-dev
1377504224421871616.topic: For the curriculum development cohort of 2025, as well as other interested educators to talk about course content and pedagogical strategies, share materials and teaching ideas etc.
1377504224421871616.description: This archived channel documents the 2025 curriculum development cohort's ongoing conversations about course design, pedagogical strategies, and teaching materials. Educators and instructors share ideas about structuring protocols and systems education, discuss session logistics, and curate resources on AI in education and innovative learning platforms. The tone is collaborative and intellectually exploratory, blending practical course coordination with deeper discussions about how to teach complex systems thinking.
1377504224421871616.guide_blurb: Archived discussions on curriculum design, teaching strategies, and educational resources from the 2025 cohort.

1379992696114122832.name: 🕸️-memory-research-group
1379992696114122832.description: The Memory Research Group is a special interest group dedicated to exploring memory across philosophical, technical, and artistic domains. Members engage in structured reading discussions (Augustine, Aquinas), share research on digital archives and memory systems, and discuss contemporary art and technology projects related to memory and storage. The group combines academic rigor with creative experimentation, featuring both synchronous meetings and asynchronous resource sharing among a small, intellectually curious community.
1379992696114122832.guide_blurb: Deep dives into memory philosophy, digital archives, and creative projects.
1379992696114122832.cadence: Every 2 weeks on Thursday at 16:00 UTC

1388223455404625951.name: sig-hosts-best-practices
1388223455404625951.topic: For hosts of special interest groups to exchange management best practices
1388223455404625951.description: This channel is a peer-to-peer knowledge exchange for Special Interest Group (SIG) hosts at Protocol Institute to discuss operational challenges, tooling decisions, and best practices. The conversation balances practical infrastructure questions (Discord vs. Zoom, event scheduling, bot development) with intellectual considerations about maintaining engaged communities over time. Participants include experienced hosts, infrastructure leads, and those building new SIGs, with a collaborative tone that treats hosting as a shared craft worth optimizing.
1388223455404625951.guide_blurb: Join if you're hosting or launching a SIG and want to learn from other hosts' experiences.

1395102280692535629.name: 🧑‍⚖️-contest-judging
1395102280692535629.description: This archived channel documents the judging process for Protocol Institute writing contests. Members share their evaluation frameworks, discuss scoring methodology, and collaborate on selecting winning entries. The conversation balances rigorous critique with accessible approaches—debating whether to read full submissions or sample pages, how to fairly evaluate different story structures, and what constitutes effective creative work.
1395102280692535629.guide_blurb: Archive of contest judging discussions & evaluation frameworks

1395426750212604045.name: 🇦🇷-buenos-aires-meetup
1395426750212604045.topic: For coordination and planning of meetup in Buenos Aires in November during Devconnect.
1395426750212604045.description: This archived channel documented the planning and execution of a Protocol Institute meetup in Buenos Aires during Devconnect week in November 2025. It hosted coordination discussions between organizers (@timber1997, @nicolascero, @_vgr) and participants around venue selection, panel scheduling, speaker recruitment (including researchers like Flavia Acosta and Sam Chua), and post-event documentation. The channel captures the intellectual vibe of interdisciplinary protocol research with practical event logistics.
1395426750212604045.guide_blurb: Archived planning channel for the Buenos Aires Devconnect meetup—check for event photos, videos, and past coordination details.

1402683646439194735.name: 🇩🇪-berlin-meetup
1402683646439194735.description: This archived channel documents a Berlin in-person meetup from October 2025 where Protocol Institute members gathered to discuss coordination mechanisms, CMM levels, and workshop ideas. The conversation reflects post-event synthesis, with participants sharing notes, summaries, and creative outputs inspired by the gathering. Content includes logistical coordination, substantive reflections on presentations, and collaborative projects that emerged from the meetup.
1402683646439194735.guide_blurb: Archived record of Oct 2025 Berlin meetup—see synthesis & creative outputs.

1405534343656636446.name: accepted-links
1405534343656636446.topic: Every link that's added to the server feed is posted here for moderation. Hit :x: to remove it from the feed. You'll also have an option to filter those domains going forward.
1405534343656636446.description: A moderated feed of curated links posted by Readwise Bot, featuring academic papers, research tools, policy resources, and cultural commentary relevant to protocol studies and technology governance. Members use reaction emojis to moderate content quality and can filter out unwanted domains. The channel reflects the Institute's interdisciplinary interests: spanning AI/ML research, institutional design, speculative fiction theory, and emerging technologies.
1405534343656636446.guide_blurb: Moderated link feed—curate the server's knowledge base by rating submissions.

1405534344348700793.name: rejected-links
1405534344348700793.topic: Every link that's filtered from the server feed is posted here in case it was a false negative. Hit :white_check_mark: to add it back to the feed. You'll also have an option to unfilter those domains going forward.
1405534344348700793.description: A moderation queue for links filtered by the server's automated feed system. The Readwise Bot posts URLs that were caught by content filters, allowing members to review false negatives and restore relevant links back to the main feed. Members can react to approve links and optionally unfilter entire domains. The channel contains academic papers, research tools, Google Docs, and occasional off-topic content that was incorrectly flagged.
1405534344348700793.guide_blurb: Review auto-filtered links and restore ones that should be in the main feed.

1410328207294726195.name: 📐-protocol-symposium
1410328207294726195.topic:
For anything and everything about the 2025 Protocol Symposium.

Share your projects and questions or look for collaborators and peers to connect with!
1410328207294726195.description: This archived channel documented the 2025 Protocol Symposium, serving as a hub for participants to share projects, seek collaborators, post reflections, and celebrate the event's conclusion. The community includes researchers, writers, and builders working across formal theory, interactive fiction, worldbuilding, and protocol design. The intellectual vibe is exploratory and collaborative—people share work-in-progress demos, blog post integrations, and thoughtful post-event reflections rather than polished presentations.
1410328207294726195.guide_blurb: Archived symposium hub—browse past projects, reflections & collaboration threads

1410351738518503495.name: 🏆-pitches-bounties-workshop
1410351738518503495.topic: In beta mode. Testing a new forum format for the pitches, bounties, and contest judging threads to improve accessibility. Upvote your favorite posts.
1410351738518503495.description: This forum channel showcases project pitches, bounty opportunities, and contest submissions from Protocol Institute members and guests. It's designed for founders, researchers, and builders to present ideas, seek collaborators, and compete for recognition and resources. The vibe is forward-thinking and opportunity-focused, with community upvoting helping surface the most compelling initiatives.
1410351738518503495.guide_blurb: Post or follow pitches, bounties & contests—upvote ideas you believe in.

1410702664089468979.name: 🥸-model-testing-temporary
1410702664089468979.description: An archived channel documenting the development and testing of a custom image generation model used for cover art and visual design. Discussion centers on prompt engineering, aesthetic direction, compositional analysis, and iterative refinement of a distinctive 'multi-perspectival, multi-scale 2.5d collage' visual style inspired by pulp magazine aesthetics. Participants include designers, model developers, and editorial staff engaging in technical and critical feedback.
1410702664089468979.guide_blurb: Archived model testing—visual design iteration & prompt engineering discussion

1422685166614085835.name: 🗺️-bridge-atlas
1422685166614085835.topic: Place to chat about the Bridge Atlas episodes and ideas!
1422685166614085835.description: This archived channel served as the discussion hub for the Bridge Atlas episode series, where community members shared thoughts, reactions, and creative ideas inspired by each episode release. The channel fostered collaborative conversation among fans and creators interested in the narrative and thematic elements of the show, maintaining an exploratory and engaged intellectual atmosphere around the project's development and impact.
1422685166614085835.guide_blurb: Archived discussions about Bridge Atlas episodes and fan theories.

1475653240837111808.name: protocol-nonfiction
1475653240837111808.topic: Talk channel for discussing how to write protocol non-fiction.
1475653240837111808.description: This channel explores the emerging genre of 'protocol nonfiction'—writing that analyzes real-world systems, technologies, and institutions through a protocol lens. Members share articles, case studies, and workshop materials examining everything from urban design and transit systems to AI architecture and civic infrastructure. The vibe is intellectually curious and genre-defining, balancing theory with concrete examples.
1475653240837111808.guide_blurb: Join to discuss writing that examines real systems through protocol analysis.

1477032718238744586.name: transcriptions
1477032718238744586.description: This channel is dedicated to sharing and discussing transcriptions of audio, video, or written content relevant to Protocol Institute's research and community interests. Members post full or partial transcripts of talks, interviews, podcasts, and presentations, enabling text-based analysis and discussion of spoken material. The channel serves researchers, note-takers, and members who prefer searchable text formats for engagement with institute content.
1477032718238744586.guide_blurb: Share transcripts of talks, interviews & media for community analysis.

1500589875617861897.name: protocol-institute-forum
1500589875617861897.description: A structured forum space for substantive discussions about protocols, methodologies, and institutional frameworks. Members pose thoughtful questions and initiate debate threads on topics ranging from technical specifications to policy implementation. The channel emphasizes evidence-based reasoning and welcomes both expert perspectives and genuine inquiry from those seeking to understand complex systems.
1500589875617861897.guide_blurb: Post questions & start discussions about protocols & institutional design.

1501309278131064872.name: editorial
1501309278131064872.topic: This is the channel for unstructured discussions about the Protocolized magazine, and pre-pitch questions/discussions.
1501309278131064872.description: A casual space for open-ended conversations about Protocolized magazine—its direction, editorial decisions, and industry trends affecting publishing. Members share news, react to developments in the media landscape, and explore pre-pitch ideas before formal submission. The tone is conversational and observational, often sparked by external events or staff musings.
1501309278131064872.guide_blurb: Casual magazine shop talk and pre-pitch discussions—follow if you're curious about our editorial process.

1501310312014549193.name: sig-talk
1501310312014549193.topic: A channel for talking about meta-SIG topics, and topics that could gel into future SIGs if there is critical mass. Feel free to sound out fellow discord members for SIGs you want to try and start one, jump on informal calls etc. We will officially charter a SIG and create a channel for it if there is enough critical mass and it is sufficiently aligned with PI mission. This channel is also where you should raise SIG management/philossophy questions if you're already hosting one.
1501310312014549193.description: A channel for discussing Special Interest Groups (SIGs) at the Protocol Institute—both meta-SIG management topics and nascent ideas seeking critical mass. Hosts debate SIG philosophy (meeting cadence, synchronous vs. async modes, group size), announce new SIGs and external projects joining PI, and members sound out peers about potential SIGs they want to launch. The vibe is exploratory and operationally focused, balancing ambitious research ambitions with pragmatic questions about how to structure effective research collectives.
1501310312014549193.guide_blurb: Follow if you're launching or hosting a SIG, or exploring a new research area.

1506119475517325424.name: new-nature
1506119475517325424.topic: A dedicated channel for discussing and evolving our institutional roadmap theme, New Nature. See here for some details: https://protocolized.summerofprotocols.com/p/inventing-new-nature
1506119475517325424.description: A research-oriented channel for investigating and developing "New Nature" — a framework for understanding structural constraints and laws that emerge from engineering choices and technological systems. Conversations are technical and philosophical, mixing formal methodology (necessary/sufficient conditions for institutional laws) with intellectual influences (Hamming, von Humboldt, Rao). Participants include researchers, AI systems with evolving memory states, and thoughtful interlocutors; the tone is exploratory rather than promotional, with emphasis on rigorous thinking over consensus.
1506119475517325424.guide_blurb: Join if you're thinking deeply about technology, constraints, and institutional design.

1506400836807561356.name: protocol-institute-network
1506400836807561356.topic: A channel for institutional partners of PI. See https://protocol-institute.org/network for details.
1506400836807561356.description: A dedicated space for institutional partners of the Protocol Institute to discuss protocol-related work, share organizational perspectives, and explore collaborative opportunities. The channel hosts representatives from universities, research centers, and other organizations working on protocol research and development. Conversation style is thoughtful and collegial, focused on substantive intellectual exchange rather than casual chat.
1506400836807561356.guide_blurb: For institutional partners to share protocol work & explore collaboration.

1507118289233514709.name: symposium-2026
1507118289233514709.topic: Channel for prospective participants in Protocol Symposium to talk about potential talk abstracts and workshop concepts. https://protocol-institute.org/symposium-2026.html
1507118289233514709.description: This channel is a collaborative space for people developing ideas for talks and workshops at Protocol Symposium 2026 (September event). Members brainstorm presentation concepts, refine abstracts, and get feedback from the community before the official call for submissions. The atmosphere is exploratory and constructive, focused on early-stage idea development rather than finished proposals.
1507118289233514709.guide_blurb: Developing a talk or workshop idea for Symposium 2026? Discuss it here.

1508175637020676259.name: 🦾-distributed-robotics
1508175637020676259.description: A space for exploring distributed robotics systems, multi-agent research, and autonomous platforms. The group discusses yakrover protocols, coordinates collaborative research sessions, shares papers on multi-agent reinforcement learning and robot integration, and debates scheduling across global timezones. Participants range from active researchers to curious newcomers interested in robotics applications from ocean monitoring to collective intelligence.
1508175637020676259.guide_blurb: Join if you're exploring distributed robotics, multi-agent systems, or autonomous platforms.
1508175637020676259.cadence: Every 2 weeks on Thursday at 16:30 UTC

1508205168661893180.name: ⏳-psychohistory
1508205168661893180.description: A special interest group focused on psychohistory—the study of history through systematic, scientific frameworks and long-term patterns. Members discuss books (monthly club format), develop projects like the Prime Radiant (an AI-powered exploration tool), and host fortnightly video calls. The vibe is intellectually curious but informal, blending theoretical readings with hands-on experimentation.
1508205168661893180.guide_blurb: Join if you're exploring psychohistory, long-term thinking, and historical systems.
1508205168661893180.cadence: Every 2 weeks on Thursday at 16:00 UTC

1515770351986938079.name: bugs-and-tests
1515770351986938079.topic: This is a channel for bug reports about PI IT infrastructure as well as for posting testing requests for new/updated features.
1515770351986938079.description: Located in the PLAZA, the community's public square, #bugs-and-tests is where members report technical issues affecting PI infrastructure (websites, Discord, bots) and request testing for new features. This is the operational backbone of the community—practical, direct, and essential for keeping systems running smoothly. Post here if you've found something broken or want to help validate updates.
1515770351986938079.guide_blurb: Report bugs in PI systems or volunteer to test new features.

1540438598212386826.name: protocol-art
1540438598212386826.description: Located in the PLAZA — the community's public-facing creative hub — #protocol-art is where members share and discuss visual work, design, and artistic expression related to Protocol Institute's intellectual culture. This is a space for finished pieces, works-in-progress, aesthetic exploration, and visual commentary that engages with the community's ideas. Expect thoughtful feedback and a mixed audience of artists, designers, and intellectually curious members.
1540438598212386826.guide_blurb: Share visual work and artistic responses to Protocol ideas.
